correctness.rationale: For all m≥2 and p,c>0 with p+c<1, the exact binomial expansion of T^(n-1) gives an n^(m-1)p^n survival envelope. Uniform Riccati bounds Q B^N≤M≤C_+ B^N hold regardless of past covariance and imply the displayed two-sided tail. The tail-sum identity verifies moments, including the critical boundary; monotonic inversion yields the quantile order. Exact rational examples checked for six n values; finite checks are not treated as the proof.

originality.rationale: The cited 2006/2007 and 2012 analyses assume binary Gilbert–Elliott losses; their pure-power or logarithmic-decay-exponent claims do not imply the explicit multiplicity-dependent log envelope in the staged channel. The finite-state 2015 model bounds maximum burst length. Closest general methodological remark is acknowledged; the added evaluated phase-transition mechanism and exact asymptotic order are not stated therein.

value.rationale: An exact infinite family of staged channel failure mechanisms shows that the widely quoted power-decay exponent alone can severely understate extreme estimator uncertainty: the tail has a diverging log^(m-1) multiplier and the high risk quantile acquires log^(m-1)/alpha inflation, while the moment threshold stays fixed. Stage multiplicity is a physically interpretable failure-depth parameter rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the consequence is quantitatively relevant to reliability and risk budgeting.
